paper.title: A Critical Review on Video-Based Continuous Sign Language Recognition

description: A video-based CSLR review covering visual feature extraction, temporal modelling, datasets, evaluation and limitations of deep-learning methods.
reason: Meets M1–M3 as a dedicated CSLR review. Table 2 compares multiple continuous-recognition architectures, datasets, reported WER and trade-offs, including multi-stream CNN–LSTM–HMM and staged-optimization approaches.

M1.reason: Abstract and body explicitly review recent CSLR advances.

M2.reason: Table2 provides a direct comparison of several prior continuous recognition studies.

M3.reason: RGB video-based models are the subject of Table2 and Section3.

evidence.passage: Table2 compares Weakly Supervised Learning with Multi-Stream CNN-LSTM-HMMs and Recurrent convolutional neural networks for continuous sign language recognition by staged optimization, including PHOENIX datasets, methods, WER and merits/demerits.

qualifying_studies: Koller et al., Weakly Supervised Learning with Multi-Stream CNN-LSTM-HMMs
Recurrent convolutional neural networks for continuous sign language recognition by staged optimization

assessments.reason: Retain for full-text assessment because review purpose and possible vision-based CSLR coverage are supported.
